# Auditing Differentially Private Code Generated by Language Models

Artifact for the paper of the same name (Osama Kamal Bela, NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for
Verifiable Coding). It contains everything needed to check or reproduce the reported numbers:
the benchmark with machine-readable audit contracts, the auditor, the generation and repair
harness, every generated program, and the scripts that produce every number and figure.

Nothing here proves a program private. The auditor searches for a counterexample and either finds
one or does not; "no violation found" is reported as exactly that.

## Layout

```
benchmark/
  tasks.yaml          16 tasks: specification, claimed (eps, delta), adjacency, neighbouring pairs
  contracts.yaml      per task: record type, value domain, size bounds, adjacency, output type
  references/         a correct implementation per task
  known_bugs/         61 planted bugs; each module records its expected detectability
                      (detectable / likely_missed / detectable_at_second_eps), written before any audit
  tasks_e8.yaml       perturbed tasks for the memorisation experiment
auditors/
  simple_auditor.py   the falsification auditor (pilot/fresh split, Clopper-Pearson, Bonferroni)
  contract.py         contract checking, capability prediction, contract-drawn pairs
  statdp_adapter.py   StatDP as a second auditor
generators/           prompt template and generation runner (Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API)
repair/               repair prompts, mechanical diagnosis, single- and multi-round repair
analysis/             one script per experiment (see below)
results/raw/          raw model responses with SHA-256 of every extracted program
results/processed/    audit outcomes, confirmations and experiment summaries
docs/TAXONOMY_RULES.md  the pre-registered defect taxonomy
```

## Setup

Python 3.11+.

```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
git clone https://github.com/cmla-psu/statdp.git third_party/statdp   # only for StatDP experiments
```

## Reproducing the paper

`analysis/make_v3_assets.py` regenerates every number (as LaTeX macros), table and figure from
`results/processed/`:

```bash
python analysis/make_v3_assets.py --paper <output-dir>
```

To re-run the pipeline from scratch:

| Step | Command |
|---|---|
| Generate (local model) | `python generators/generation_runner.py --model qwen2.5-coder:7b --base-url http://localhost:11434/v1 --samples 10` |
| Audit | `python analysis/aggregate.py` |
| Confirm detections | `python analysis/confirm_seeds.py --k 3` |
| Generic-auditor probes, planted bugs | `python analysis/e1_three_arm.py` / `--bugs` |
| Random contract pairs | `python analysis/e2_random_pairs.py` |
| Prior-work bugs (StatDP suite) | `python analysis/e9_prior_bugs.py` |
| Second auditor | `python analysis/cross_auditor.py` |
| Hosted models | `run_e12_models.ps1` (needs `GEMINI_API_KEY`) |
| Taxonomy worksheet / annotation | `python analysis/e13_taxonomy_worksheet.py`, `python analysis/e13_annotate_llm.py` |
| Repair | `python repair/repair_runner.py`, `python repair/multi_round.py` |
| Memorisation | `python analysis/e8_validate.py`, `python analysis/e8_report.py` |

The audit deliberately draws fresh randomness on every run. Re-running reproduces the set of
confirmed violations, not every marginal initial detection; the archived outcomes let every
reported number be checked exactly.

API keys are read from an environment variable or a file in your home directory, never from the
repository (`generators/apikey.py`).
